sources.fact: Testicles are usually kept at about 35 C, about two degrees below body temperature; the cremaster muscle draws them closer for warmth or away to cool; a few degrees of extra heat can inhibit sperm production; laptop use adds heat
Hot tubs and heat lower sperm count, motility and shape; fertility usually returns after the heat stops (takes months)
Laptop use on the lap raises scrotal temperature

post.instagram_caption:
Your body has its own cooling system. Who knew? ❄️

Testicles work best about two degrees cooler than the rest of the body. When it's cold they pull up closer for warmth, and when it's hot they drop down to cool off.

That's why regular hot tubs, and laptops on your lap, can lower sperm count for a while.

Sources: McGill Office for Science and Society, Turek Clinic, Columbia Go Ask Alice.
